canonical_identity.title: Evolution of Detection Performance Throughout the Online Lifespan of Synthetic Images

claims.claim: Introduction contributions and sections4.4–4.8 make calibration, in-the-wild discrimination and temporal detector degradation primary study questions, beyond validating the FOSID resource.

Time-ordered copies of four fact-checked seed images are split into quarters. Basic images from Q1 versus Q4 are evaluated using balanced accuracy at an EER threshold and AUC, averaged over five real-image datasets.
FOSID includes four seed lineages and a small unique-image set; reported temporal evidence is observational, not a general causal estimate for elapsed time.

caveats: Author manuscript v1 is not asserted byte-equivalent to Springer final.
Table1 reports3070total URLs, whereas the four displayed TotalURLs cells678+772+808+745 sum to3003; preserve both.
Table5 Rine/PatchCraft displayed All scores appear interchanged relative to Table4; do not silently repair method labels.

§4.8 narrative says nine BA declines, but rounded Table6 cells show eight negative BA differences, one zero(Dire), and three positive values; ten negative AUC differences are supported. Hidden unrounded values were not available.
Overall -2.6%/-3.2% are reported mean relative changes, not percentage-point drops.

Four deliberately selected seed lineages, observational copy histories and nonuniform post-processing do not identify a universal causal effect of elapsed time. EER thresholds and best-of25pretrained models are evaluation choices, not an independently calibrated deployment claim.
